solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Worry about pet in case of bullets

indicators.note: about means the worry word goes round the stroking word

parts.note: to worry is to care, as in fret
to pet is to touch or stroke

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about an animal kept in an ammunition box.
explanation.walkthrough: A cartouche is an old term for a soldier's cartridge box; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a cartouche was a paper cartridge or the soldier's box holding such cartridges.

clue.text: Younger son acted strangely

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of the action word are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A boy who behaved oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cadet's old sense is a younger son of a family, the one not inheriting.
explanation.definitionFit: In its traditional sense a cadet is a younger son or a junior branch of a family.

clue.text: Evidence of sale about chair heard

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: RE means about and to seat is to chair, so together re-seat

explanation.surface: A dispute over a chair sale, with proof of purchase overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) and SEAT (chair) make RE-SEAT, which said aloud matches the word for proof of purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the slip that proves goods were bought and paid for.

clue.text: Protestant to roam in Arabian state

indicators.note: in means the roaming word is placed inside the Arabian country

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula
to range is to roam

explanation.surface: A Protestant traveller wandering through the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orangeman is a member of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternal society in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangemen belong to the Orange Order, a Protestant society chiefly in Ulster.

clue.text: One describes how Parisian upset ecclesiastical tribunal

parts.note: comment is French for how

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the court's name upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the Rota is the Roman Catholic Church's appeal court

explanation.surface: A Frenchman explains how a church court was overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman Rota is the Vatican's high court; 'upset' turns ROTA to ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator is someone who describes events, as at a sports match.

clue.text: Mischievous being lines up female

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the lines word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: EL is the US elevated railway, so lines; reversed it gives LE

explanation.surface: An imp lines up a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small sprite from folklore given to playing tricks.

clue.text: Excellent R&B makes you harsh and bitter

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
the two letters of the music genre R&B, rhythm and blues

explanation.surface: Even great rhythm and blues can leave a sour taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare variant of acerbic, sharp and sour in taste or manner.

clue.text: First to alter attitude taken over fabulous writer

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word
taken over means the attitude word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: A writer of fables changing his stance first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means writing fables, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek teller of fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Greek character embraced by female creature

indicators.note: embraced by means the Greek letter sits inside the woman's name

parts.note: Edna is a woman's name
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man hugged by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Noteworthy personality of British artist and German one

parts.note: Max Ernst was a German surrealist artist
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A celebrity made of a British painter and a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noteworthy' is a pun: Leonard Bernstein was a man of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein, composer of West Side Story, was a famous figure in music.

clue.text: Failed medical brings attack

indicators.note: something failed has gone wrong, so the following word's letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Flunking a medical sets off an angry tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim against something is to attack it in loud rhetorical speech.

clue.text: Trawlerman rounds cape, one successful on board

indicators.note: rounds means the fisherman word goes around the cape letter

parts.note: a trawlerman is a fisher
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A fishing boat's skipper sails round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby Fischer was the American world chess champion; 'on board' means at the chessboard, not aboard the trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby Fischer won the world chess championship in 1972, a star of the chessboard.

clue.text: Square circle in the town

parts.note: a T-square, the draughtsman's tool, gives the letter T
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson about squares and circles in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tring is a small English market town in Hertfordshire.

clue.text: Beaten Peru side includes current play-maker

indicators.note: includes means the shuffled letters take in the current letter
beaten suggests a team knocked about, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A football report: a beaten Peruvian team still has a playmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' shuffles PERU SIDE into EURIPDES, and 'includes' puts I inside it. 'Play-maker' looks like football but means a writer of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the great tragic dramatists of ancient Athens, a writer of plays.

clue.text: You'll find Harris in one shivering whatever the weather

indicators.note: shivering suggests trembling and jumbling, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Harris tweed wearer shivers outdoors in any weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Come rain or shine is the idiom for whatever the weather or conditions.

clue.text: Known to be impossible

definitions.meaning: when a secret is ... it has become known
an idea that is ... is ruled ..., not possible

explanation.definitionFit: Out means revealed, as in the secret is out, and also excluded, as in that option is out.

clue.text: Islanders have nothing for leader of countrymen

indicators.note: for leader of means the first letter is replaced by the nothing letter

parts.note: Arcadians are idealised rustics, country folk of pastoral Arcadia
O is the zero figure, nothing

explanation.surface: Islanders are leaderless country folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcadians are people from Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcadians are inhabitants of Orkney, an archipelago north of Scotland.

clue.text: Get into college having pranged ultimate car

indicators.note: pranged is British slang for crashed, so the car's letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A student crashes a fancy car on the way to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prang' is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To matriculate is to enrol formally as a member of a university or college.

clue.text: Galloping Steppe duo now at full pace

indicators.note: galloping suggests horses charging about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Two riders gallop across the steppe at full speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to speed means running at full rate, having reached operating pace.

clue.text: Dresser after government job

parts.note: a dresser is a cabinet, a piece of furniture
post is the Latin prefix for after

explanation.surface: Someone seeking a furniture job, or a minister angling for promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet post is a ministerial position in a government's inner cabinet.

clue.text: Cry, finding tissue

definitions.meaning: the fatty layer under a whale's skin

explanation.definitionFit: Blubber is both a verb for sobbing loudly and the noun for a whale's fat layer.

clue.text: Knowledge good to get with vacant expression

indicators.note: vacant means the word is emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A clever person gets along with someone wearing a blank look.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British informal for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British slang for information or inside knowledge.

clue.text: Pineapple class admits unmarried men

indicators.note: admits means the class word lets the other piece inside

parts.note: a grade is a class or rank

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, so unmarried takes it away

explanation.surface: A pineapple-growing class lets in some bachelors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pineapple' is old military slang for a hand grenade, from its ridged shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple was soldiers' slang for a hand bomb because of its segmented casing.

clue.text: Doctor keeping strange company added message for musicians

indicators.note: keeping means the doctor word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: rum is British informal for strange
PS, postscript, is a message added to a letter

explanation.surface: A doctor with odd colleagues tacks a note on the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum corps is a marching band of drummers and buglers, a body of musicians.

clue.text: Bird died in flock

parts.note: a crow is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird perishes among its flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large gathering of people, like a flock or throng.

clue.text: Returning in plane I see Italian location

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Flying home, a passenger spots somewhere in Italy from the window.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a Tuscan city in Italy famous for its Palio horse race.

clue.text: Examination requiring much bookwork?

parts.note: it reads like a school exam needing study, but means an inspection of account books

explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of an organisation's financial accounts and books.

clue.text: One doctor stood up to provide name

parts.note: a means one
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
rose means stood up

explanation.surface: A single doctor rose to offer a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrose is a man's given name, as borne by Saint Ambrose of Milan.

clue.text: Greek goddess without husband for long time

indicators.note: without means the husband letter is dropped

parts.note: Hera is queen of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess left without her husband for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Hera's husband was Zeus, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history.

clue.text: Anger to weigh down country

parts.note: ire is anger
to land someone with a task is to burden or weigh them down

explanation.surface: Rage that bears heavily on a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is the island nation west of Great Britain.

clue.text: Rushes back for musical instrument

indicators.note: back means the word for rushes is read backwards

parts.note: to dart is to rush

explanation.surface: A musician dashes back to fetch a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: A Strad is a Stradivarius violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is short for a Stradivarius, a violin or cello by Antonio Stradivari.

clue.text: Moving about meant carrying correct change

indicators.note: carrying means the shuffled letters hold another word inside
moving about means the letters of the next word are shifted around

parts.note: to mend is to correct or put right

explanation.surface: A shifting meaning carries a correction for a revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving about' rearranges the letters into AMENT, and 'carrying' sets the repair word just after the A; 'correct' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to a text, law or motion.
